evidence: Receiving DO2 11.9 mg/L at 50.0 h falling to 5.9 mg/L at 52.0 h, sustained over 10 readings
Source batches 1-3 hold DO2 ~10.5-11.5 mg/L at 52 h; receiving trajectory is a marked divergence
Receiving P(48h)=2.65 g/L vs source 2.98-3.06 g/L (~13% behind)

Forward model: combined gives 299 kg product, min DO 2.23 mg/L, 4/5 feasible; keep 243 kg, min DO 2.09, 3/5 feasible; increase_air alone infeasible (min DO 1.95, 0.4 h below limit); reduce_feed 271 kg, min DO 2.49
args.rationale: Receiving fermentation shows a sustained oxygen-transfer collapse (DO2 11.9 to 5.9 mg/L over 50.0-52.0 h, far below all three source trajectories at the same age) with product already ~13% behind sources. The combined intervention (feed 0.8x, air 1.15x) is the only bounded action that both relieves the oxygen deficit and retains growth: the forward model predicts the highest feasible product mass (299 kg vs 243 kg for keep) with min DO 2.23 mg/L above the 2.0 limit and 4/5 feasible sensitivity members. Air increase alone is predicted infeasible (min DO 1.95, 0.4 h below limit); feed reduction alone is safe but yields less product (271 kg). Stop is rejected as it counts zero production.
args.uncertainty: Forward model is a nominal source-calibrated approximation, not the hidden receiving realization; sensitivity members for combined span min DO 1.48-3.70 mg/L and product 215-598 kg, so oxygen compliance is not guaranteed. DO sensor readings are noisy but the 10-point sustained decline is unambiguous. Post-intervention DO should be monitored; if DO trends below ~2.5 mg/L, escalate to strong_feed_reduction. The exact cause (transfer capacity loss vs feed excess) is inferred, not measured.
